Definition: from G4119; moreover (besides), i.e. albeit, save that, rather, yet:--but (rather), except, nevertheless, notwithstanding, save, than.
BiblicalUsage: Plen is a little word — moreover, but, nevertheless, save that — the hinge a sentence turns on. Jesus prays, nevertheless not my will, but Thine, be done, in Luke 22:42 and Matthew 26:39. And Paul says, what then, notwithstanding, every way Christ is preached, in Philippians 1:18.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the smallest word in the Bible can carry the biggest surrender — nevertheless.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
